label: copy-phase input e or f (fed-back e/f)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively in the copy phase (t > L) when the fed-back input token is e or f (f carries ~72% of mass, e ~28%); this captures 99.9% of activation mass. Never fires in the original phase (47 stray steps) or on the delimiter, and essentially never on other input tokens. Magnitude: f > e; activation rate and size grow with recall_idx/position in the copy phase (rate 3% at recall_idx 1 vs 5.5% at 8 overall), and top activations are f late in the copy. Precision is only ~0.65: about a third of copy-phase e/f inputs, especially early ones, do not fire, and no simple history variable (recall_idx, to_go, in_count) cleanly separates them.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: f, e, c, x, n, 0; least: l, q, d, u) and the next token to output (most: k, p, d, w, s, v; least: 0, n, e, f); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=7 & t=3, L=9 & t=3.
